title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Section 6 (Rules to Regulate Environmental Pollution)

content.overview: Section 6 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the Central Government to make rules in respect of all or any of the matters referred to in section 3. Rules may address standards of environmental quality, maximum allowable concentration of pollutants, procedures for handling hazardous substances, prohibition and restriction on location of industries, and related regulatory subjects as the section enumerates. Section 6 is the principal rule-making base for much of the EPA subordinate legislation, including aspects of the EIA framework.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is there a Central rule under s. 6? (2) Which s. 3 matter does it address? (3) Does the rule bind the facts (standards, hazardous handling, location restrictions)?
content.study:
s. 6 is rule-making power tied to s. 3 matters. Always verify the specific rule and notification text rather than inventing standards.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Rule-making power
sections.body: Central Government may make rules for all or any matters referred to in s. 3.

sections.heading: Illustrative subjects
sections.body: Standards of quality; maximum allowable concentration of environmental pollutants; procedures and safeguards for handling hazardous substances; prohibition/restriction on location of industries and carrying on of processes/operations — as enumerated.

sections.heading: Link to s. 3
sections.body: Rules operationalise the general measures power in s. 3.

sections.heading: Compliance
sections.body: Contravention of rules attracts the Act's penalty and enforcement scheme (including s. 15).

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the rule, its s. 3 link, and the factual obligation it creates.

examples.title: Standards rule
examples.body: A Central rule under s. 6 fixes emission standards for a process — operators must comply; breach feeds s. 7/s. 15 analysis.

hypotheticals.question: Can standards exist without a s. 6 rule?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 6 is the principal rule-making route for matters in s. 3; specific obligations usually rest on notified rules and orders.

distinctions.title: s. 6 rules vs s. 3 measures
distinctions.right: General power to take all measures necessary or expedient for environmental protection.

misconceptions.trap: s. 6 itself lists every numerical standard.
misconceptions.correction: s. 6 authorises rules; the numerical standards appear in the rules and notifications made thereunder.
